questions.q: Which organ is shown in this slide?
questions.explain: Glomeruli surrounded by many tubule profiles are the visible clue.
questions.alt: Low-power view of round glomerular tufts among many round tubule profiles, with a larger pale vessel near the centre.

questions.q: What are the round tufts surrounded by a pale space?
questions.explain: Each renal corpuscle is a glomerular tuft inside Bowman's capsule.
questions.alt: Low-power view of round glomerular tufts among many round tubule profiles, with a larger pale vessel near the centre.

questions.q: How can renal cortex be told from medulla?
options: The cortex contains glomeruli; the medulla does not
The cortex contains only collecting ducts
questions.explain: Glomeruli are found only in the cortex.
questions.alt: Low-power view of round glomerular tufts among many round tubule profiles, with a larger pale vessel near the centre.

questions.q: Which specialised epithelial cells form the visceral layer of Bowman's capsule and wrap around glomerular capillaries?
questions.explain: Podocytes are specialised epithelial cells whose interdigitating foot processes form filtration slits over the glomerular capillaries.

questions.q: A renal cortical tubule has tall cuboidal cells with a prominent apical brush border, making its lumen appear relatively narrow and fuzzy. Which segment is shown?
options: Thin limb of loop of Henle
questions.explain: The proximal convoluted tubule has abundant apical microvilli forming a brush border, reflecting its major role in reabsorption.

questions.q: Which feature helps distinguish a distal convoluted tubule from a proximal convoluted tubule in a routine renal cortical section?
options: A clearer, wider lumen and absence of a prominent brush border
A thick apical brush border and indistinct lumen
A lumen consistently filled with erythrocytes
questions.explain: Distal convoluted tubules have fewer microvilli and a more distinct, open lumen than proximal convoluted tubules.

questions.q: Which specialised region of the distal tubule forms part of the juxtaglomerular apparatus and senses tubular sodium chloride delivery?
questions.explain: Macula densa cells are specialised epithelial cells near the vascular pole that detect tubular NaCl and participate in tubuloglomerular feedback.

questions.q: The renal pelvis and ureter must accommodate changes in urine volume while protecting underlying tissues from urine. Which epithelium provides this lining?
questions.explain: Urothelium is a specialised stretchable epithelium lining the renal calyces, pelvis, ureters and urinary bladder; its superficial umbrella cells form a protective barrier.
